mechanism_narrative: A positive month-over-month change in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) indicates strengthening labor market conditions, which typically boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in 60% or more of months with positive MoM PAYEMS growth (>=0.5%).

mechanism_narrative: A decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4.5% signals a tight labor market, which typically precedes stronger economic growth and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in 60% or more of instances where UNRATE < 4.5%.

mechanism_narrative: The joint increase in industrial production (INDPRO) and housing starts (HOUST) indicates robust economic momentum across manufacturing and construction sectors, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal (both INDPRO and HOUST rising) fails to predict positive 20-day returns in 60% or more of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) exceeding 0.25% in the past month signals an active monetary tightening cycle, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in 60% or more of instances where FEDFUNDS rises > 0.25% in 1 month.

mechanism_narrative: When the year-over-year change in CPI (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 2.5%, it signals persistent inflation, prompting the Federal Reserve to tighten policy and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in 60% or more of instances where CPIAUCSL > 2.5% YoY.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in industrial production (INDPRO) over the past three months indicates strengthening economic activity, which typically leads to higher corporate profits and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in 60% or more of months with positive 3-month INDPRO growth.

mechanism_narrative: When both inflation (CPIAUCSL) and the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) are elevated (CPIAUCSL > 2.5% YoY and FEDFUNDS > 2.0%), it signals a high-inflation, tight-monetary regime that typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal (CPIAUCSL > 2.5% YoY and FEDFUNDS > 2.0%) fails to predict negative 20-day returns in 60% or more of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A strong month-over-month increase in retail sales (RSAFS) indicates robust consumer spending, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in 60% or more of months with positive MoM RSAFS growth (>=0.5%).
